title: Noahic Lineages of Russia, Armenia, the Goths, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, Germany, Spain, Gaul & Italy

nodes.name: Slavs (Norici) & Rus' — Lot of Japheth
nodes.role: Japhethic Ancestors of the Russians, Varangians & Slavic Nations
nodes.notes: Opening genealogy of the Rus' Primary Chronicle: after the Flood, Japheth received the northern/western rivers (Danube, Dnieper, Volga, Baltic/Varangian Sea), explicitly numbering Rus', Varangians, Slavs (Norici), Moravians, Czechs, White Croats, Serbs, Polyanians, Derevlians & Poles (Lyakhs) in the race of Japheth.

nodes.name: Kiy, Shchek, Khoriv & Sister Lybed' (Founders of Kiev)
nodes.era: Early Polyanian Princes (Russian Primary Chronicle p. 55)
nodes.role: Legendary Eponymous Founders of Kiev
nodes.notes: Three Polyanian Slavic brothers Kiy, Shchek, Khoriv and sister Lybed' founded Kiev on the Dnieper; Lyakh brothers Radim & Vyatko founded the Radimichians & Vyatichians.

nodes.name: Rurik (+ Sineus & Truvor, 862 CE) → Oleg & Igor' (+ St. Olga of Kiev)
nodes.role: Varangian-Japhethic Founders of the Rurikid Dynasty
nodes.notes: Varangian prince Rurik (expressly placed under the race of Japheth in the Primary Chronicle p. 52) settled Novgorod with brothers Sineus & Truvor (862 CE); regent Oleg united Novgorod & Kiev for Rurik's son Igor' and St. Olga of Pskov.

nodes.name: Svyatoslav I of Kiev (Son of Igor' & Olga)
nodes.role: Warrior Prince of Kievan Rus'
nodes.notes: Son of Igor' and St. Olga; campaigned across the Volga, Khazaria, and the Danube; father of Vladimir the Great.

nodes.name: St. Vladimir the Great of Kiev (Baptized Kievan Rus', 988 CE)
nodes.role: Grand Prince of Kiev
nodes.notes: Grandson of Rurik and St. Olga; married Byzantine Princess Anna Porphyrogenita and established Christianity across Rus' in 988 CE.

nodes.name: Yaroslav the Wise (1019–1054 CE) → Royal Houses of Rus', France, Norway & Hungary
nodes.role: Grand Prince of Kiev & Pan-European Ancestor
nodes.notes: Son of St. Vladimir; linked the Rurikid line into Western & Northern European monarchies through his daughters Anne of Kiev (Queen of France), Anastasia (Hungary) & Elisiv (Norway).

nodes.name: Hayk Nahapet (Patriarch of Armenia, Slayer of Bel/Nimrod)
nodes.role: Progenitor of the Armenian Nation
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.5-11
nodes.notes: Movses Khorenatsi traces Hayk from Noah -> Japheth -> Gomer -> Tiras -> Togarmah (Torgom), describing his refusal to serve the tyrant Bel (Nimrod) at Babel and his victory over Bel near Lake Van.

nodes.name: Aramaneak → Aramayis → Amasia → Gegham → Harma → Aram (Eponym of Armenia) → Ara the Handsome
nodes.role: Early Patriarchal Chiefs of Armenia
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.12-15
nodes.notes: Direct Haykid generational succession in Movses Khorenatsi leading through Aram (from whom neighbors named Armenia) to Ara the Handsome, contemporary of Assyrian queen Semiramis.

nodes.name: Shambat (Jewish Noble Exiled by Nebuchadnezzar) → Armenian Bagratuni Dynasty
nodes.era: 6th c. BCE onward (Movses Khorenatsi I.22 & II.3)
nodes.role: Judeo-Armenian Ancestor of the Bagratuni & Bagrationi Houses
sources: Movses Khorenatsi History of Armenia I.22, II.3
nodes.notes: Khorenatsi records that Armenian king Hracheay brought a prominent Jewish captive named Shambat (Smbat) from Nebuchadnezzar's Babylonian exile — establishing the Armenian Bagratuni & Georgian Bagrationi royal claim.

nodes.name: Goths / Scythians (Berig → Filimer) — Race of Magog
nodes.role: Japhethic Origin of the Gothic & Scythian Peoples
nodes.notes: Jordanes (following Josephus) connects the Scythian & Gothic peoples to Magog son of Japheth and recounts King Berig leading three ships of Goths from Scandza across the Baltic to Gothiscandza, followed by Filimer to Oium.

nodes.name: Gapt (Gaut) → Amal (Amali) → Hermanaric → Theoderic the Great (Ostrogoths) & Alaric I (Visigoths)
nodes.role: Royal Ostrogothic Amali & Visigothic Balthi Lines
nodes.notes: Complete royal genealogy of the Gothic Amali from Gapt (Gaut) -> Hulmul -> Augis -> Amal -> Ostrogotha -> Achiulf -> Hermanaric & Vandalarius -> Thiudimer -> Theoderic the Great, alongside Alaric I of the Visigoths.

nodes.name: Baath (King of Scythia) → Fenius Farsa (Inventor of Letters at Shinar/Babel)
nodes.era: Post-Babel Scythia (Annals of the Four Masters; O'Hart pp. 31-34)
nodes.role: Magogian Patriarch of Gaelic & Scythian Learning
sources: O'Hart Irish Pedigrees Part I pp. 31-35
nodes.notes: O'Hart traces the stem of the Irish nation directly from Adam -> Seth -> ... -> Noah -> Japheth -> Magog -> Baath (King of Scythia) -> Fenius Farsa, who established a school of the 72 languages on the plain of Shinar after Babel.

nodes.name: Niul (+ Scota, Dau. of Pharaoh; Friend of Moses!) → Gaodhal Glas (Gael) → Asruth → Sruth → Heber Scot
nodes.role: Egyptian-Milesian Bridge & Eponym of the Gaels
sources: O'Hart Irish Pedigrees Part I pp. 6, 34-35
nodes.notes: Fenius Farsa's younger son Niul was invited to Egypt by Pharaoh, married Princess Scota, befriended Moses & the Israelites at the Red Sea, and begat Gaodhal Glas (Gael), father of the Goidelic language and line through Asruth, Sruth & Heber Scot.

nodes.name: Breoghan (Brigus of Spain) → Bile → Milesius of Spain (Galamh)
nodes.role: Progenitor of the Milesian High Kings of Ireland
sources: O'Hart Irish Pedigrees Part I pp. 29-35
nodes.notes: O'Hart generations #34-36 from Adam: Breoghan (Brigus, builder of Brigantia in Spain) -> Bile -> Galamh / Milesius of Spain, who married a second Pharaoh's daughter Scota.

nodes.name: Heber, Heremon, Ir & Uncle Ith (Milesian Monarchs of Ireland)
nodes.role: Joint Progenitors of the Major Irish & Scottish Houses
sources: O'Hart Irish Pedigrees Part I pp. 49-84
nodes.notes: Milesius's sons Heber (Munster lines), Heremon (Connacht, Leinster, High Kings & Dal Riada Scots), and Ir (Ulster), alongside uncle Ith, established the Milesian roll of Irish monarchs.

nodes.name: Conn of the Hundred Battles → Niall of the Nine Hostages (Uí Néill) & Brian Boru (Munster)
nodes.role: Historic High Kings of Ireland from Heremon & Heber
nodes.notes: Traces Heremon's line to Conn of the Hundred Battles -> Niall of the Nine Hostages (Uí Néill) and Heber's line to Brian Boru (d. 1014 CE) & MacCarthy/O'Brien families.

nodes.name: Cruithne (Founder of the Picts) → 7 Sons Dividing Alba (Fib, Fidach, Floclaid, Fortrenn, Got, Ce, Circinn)
nodes.role: Eponymous Ancestor of the Picts of Alba (Scotland)
sources: Skene Chronicles of the Picts & Scots pp. 209-252
nodes.notes: The Pictish Chronicle derives both Scots and Picts from Scythia/Albani (Noah -> Japheth -> Magog/Gomer), recording Cruithne and his seven sons giving their names to the seven provinces of Pictish Scotland.

nodes.name: Fergus Mor mac Erc (King of Dal Riada, 498 CE) → Kenneth MacAlpin (1st King of Scots & Picts, 843 CE)
nodes.role: Unifier of the Picts & Scots into the Scottish Crown
sources: Skene Chronicles of the Picts & Scots pp. cx, 44
nodes.notes: Fergus Mor mac Erc crossed from Irish Dal Riada (Heremon's Milesian line) to Argyll in 498 CE; his descendant Cináed mac Ailpín (Kenneth MacAlpin) united the Scottish and Pictish kingdoms in 843 CE.

nodes.name: Cunedda → Cadwaladr → Rhodri Mawr → Hywel Dda → Llywelyn the Great (Princes of Wales)
nodes.era: 5th–13th c. CE (Brut y Tywysogion; Four Ancient Books of Wales)
nodes.role: Welsh Royal Succession Descended from Brutus of Troy & Camber
sources: Skene Four Ancient Books of Wales
nodes.notes: Follows the Welsh chronicle tradition from Cunedda Wledig and Cadwaladr the Blessed through Rhodri Mawr (the Great), lawgiver Hywel Dda, Gruffudd ap Rhys & Llywelyn the Great, tracing Welsh sovereignty back to Brutus of Troy & Camber.

nodes.name: Ashkenaz = Tuisco / Tuisto (1st King of Germany)
nodes.role: Japhethic Patriarch of Germanic Peoples in Classical Chronography
nodes.notes: Anderson Table p. 464 identifies Japheth's grandson Ashkenaz (Askanez) with Tacitus & Aventinus's Tuisco/Tuisto, pioneer ruler near the Tanais and Germany.

nodes.name: Tubal (Progenitor of Iberia / Ancient Kings of Spain)
nodes.role: Japhethic Founder of the Iberians of Spain
nodes.notes: Josephus Antiquities I.6.1 identifies Tubal son of Japheth with the Iberi ('Thobelites'), later joined in royal chronologies to the ancient kingdoms of Spain.

nodes.name: Gomer / Samothes (Progenitor of Gauls / Celts / Cimbri)
nodes.era: Post-Flood Gaul & Britain (Josephus Ant. I.6.1; Anderson 1732 p. 464)
nodes.role: Japhethic Patriarch of the Cimmerians, Cimbri, Celts & Gauls
nodes.notes: Josephus states 'Gomer founded those whom the Greeks now call Galatians [Gauls], but were then called Gomerites'; Anderson links Gomer (Cimbri) and his son Samothes/Meshech to the Celts.

nodes.name: Noah = Janus / Ogyges → Sabatius Saga → Italus (Ancient Kings of Italy / Tuscany)
nodes.era: Annius / Anderson Chronography (1732 Table CCCCXXIV p. 702)
nodes.role: Renaissance-Baroque Noahic Synchronization of Pre-Roman Italy
sources: James Anderson Royal Genealogies (1732 Table CCCCXXIV p. 702)
nodes.notes: Anderson Table CCCCXXIV places Noah (identified as Janus / Ogyges) planting colonies in Italy with Gomer & Kittim, succeeded by Sabatius Saga and the ancient Kings of Tuscany & Italy.
